This research explores the efficacy of applying label smoothing regularization as a preventative measure against such attacks on object detectors. Our experiments indicate that, when a standard Softmax function is used for classification within neural network architectures for object detection—as current state-of-the-models do—employing smooth labels yields a clear benefit in both robustness and accuracy. As an increasing number of distributed energy resources (DERs) are integrated with utility-scale photovoltaic systems, oscillations driven by power electronics have become a significant challenge to grid stability. This analysis examines the influence of wide-bandwidth active power control on low-frequency power oscillations, employing a strategy designed for grid-forming inverters deployed with grid-following converters. Findings demonstrate that wide-bandwidth active power control effectively suppresses low-frequency oscillations by restricting variations in active power injection caused by fluctuations in grid voltage magnitude.

Furthermore, employing wide-bandwidth active power control to suppress oscillations provides a flexible solution that avoids recalibrating settings for grid-following PV inverter standards, maintaining its efficacy even with power factor levels close to unity.
